the issuing office.

in Shanghai, there are some - not more than 2% to 3% -
who are in possession of "Staatenlose" passports issued
by the German home authorities. These documents are
issued to persons residing in the Reich unable to
substantiate their German nationality and are valid for
one year only, after which period they are not renewable.

Russian and Polish origin.

When the validity of these documents expires, the
holders lose all claim to any form of protection from

日期：1939年7月26日。
主题：中欧犹太人——身份证明文件。
制作人：D.S. Pitts 转呈人：C. Crawford 警司

现随函附上由九江路190号“国际委员会”（I.C.）难民救济办公室签发给 Siegfried FREUND 的身份证明文件，编号为 002/39。Freund 原为德国公民（至1935年止），现已丧失其国籍。

随附该文件的还有签发办公室荣誉秘书兼财务主管 P. KORNOR 先生的一份函件。

在抵达上海的众多犹太难民中，有一部分人——不超过2%至3%——持有德国内政当局签发的“无国籍”（Staatenlose）护照。这些文件签发给居住在帝国境内但无法证明其德国国籍的人士，有效期仅为一年，期满后不予续期。受此影响最大的是具有俄罗斯和波兰血统的犹太人。

当这些文件的有效期届满时，持有人将失去德国当局任何形式的保护主张权，实际上成为无国籍人士。

由“国际委员会”救济基金签发的文件仅仅是一份身份证明书，因此不具备护照效力。

该文件的持有人请求警方予以背书，从而承认其有效性。

如果给予所需的背书，可以确信其他不时持有此类文件的人也会提出类似请求

就我看来，对该文件进行背书并无多大益处，因为它只能在上海用于表明持证人身份，而毫无疑问，在“国际委员会”救济组织成为完全获认可的机构之前，领事团不会承认该文件。
在处理这些来自欧洲的新来者时，不可忽视一个至关重要的事实，即例如德国的商人有随身携带护照以便在本国进行身份识别的习惯。上海并不存在这种情况，虽然也许建议每位本地居民都能证明自己（她）的身份，但除非认为此举有助于促进“国际委员会”的良好工作，否则警方似乎没有必要对“国际委员会”签发的文件进行背书。

J. A. Picca
D. S.

指挥官

pages.en:
Provisional Arrangement Regarding Entry into Shanghai of
Central European Refugees.

1. Only those Central European Refugees who are recognized
to be in possession of not less than U.S.$400 and U.S.$100 per head
respectively in case of an adult and child of less than 13 years
of age or its equivalent in foreign currency to be available in
Shanghai or who are in possession of an entry permit provided for
under Article 2, and issued by one of the three following Authori-
ties, viz: the Japanese Consulate-General, the Council of the
International Settlement, or the Authorities of the French Con-
cession, will be permitted to enter Shanghai. It is required by
the Japanese Authorities that those incoming Refugees who wish to
reside in that part of the International Settlement which is under
Japanese occupation must so register, through the Committee for
the Assistance of European Jewish Refugees, at the Japanese Naval
authorities in Shanghai.

2. The application for entry permit by reason of
(a) immediate family relation (i.e. parents, husband
wife or children) to Refugees of certified finan-
cial competency resident in Shanghai, or
(b) an employment contract with a party in Shanghai,
or
(c) intention to contract marriage with a party resident
in Shanghai,
should be made through the Committee for the Assistance of Euro-
pean Jewish Refugees in Shanghai to one of the three Authorities
according to where the local refugee applicant resides, with the
understanding that the decision on issuing permit rests entirely
with the discretion of the respective Authorities.

关于中欧难民进入上海的临时安排。

1. 只有被确认拥有不少于400美元（成人）及100美元（13岁以下儿童）或等值外币并在上海可用，或持有根据第2条规定由以下三个当局之一签发的入境许可证的中欧难民，方准进入上海。这三个当局分别是：日本总领事馆、国际租界工部局或法租界当局。日本当局要求，希望居住在国际租界日军占领区的入境难民必须通过欧洲犹太难民援助委员会向上海日本海军当局登记。

2. 因以下原因申请入境许可证：
(a) 与居住在上海且经认证具备财务能力的难民有直系亲属关系（即父母、丈夫、妻子或子女），或
(b) 与上海一方签订雇佣合同，或
(c) 打算与居住在上海的一方结婚，
应根据当地难民申请人居住地，通过上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会向三个当局之一提出申请，须知是否签发许可证完全取决于各当局的裁量权。

Special Branch,
January 10, 19

Central European Refugees - Recent arrivals via Siberia
------------------------------------------------------------------

During the past two months or so it has come to the notice of
this office that a small number of Central European Jewish refugees
have been arriving in Shanghai via Siberia and the D.K.K. sea-route
from Dairen not in possession of Immigration Certificates issued by
the Police. In certain instances money has been deposited in Shanghai
with the Committee on behalf of these people and the permits issued by
the Police. The permits are then sent to Europe to the person(s) con-
cerned, but in the cases coming to the notice of the Police the per-
son(s) concerned are arriving in Shanghai before the permits reach the
town in question in Europe.

The immigrants then register at this office and naturally re-
quest to be allowed to take possession of the money deposited for them.
As the certificates are not produced their requests for the return of
the deposits have been met with refusals. In each instance the immi-
grant(s) have been told to secure possession of the certificates when
permission will be given for them to secure their funds.

This state of affairs is apparently brought about by the apathe-
tical attitude of the D.K.K. Line in regard to the Council's regulations
dated October 22, 1939. The steamship company is obviously not asking
refugees to produce their permits before steamer tickets are issued.
In this connection I would also point out that a few instances have
occurred recently where refugees have arrived in Shanghai either with
no permits at all or with permits the validity of which had expired.
Without exception the immigrants concerned arrived via Siberia and the
D.K.K. sea-route ex Dairen.

In view of the fact that some of the immigrants who have money
deposited in Shanghai with the Committee urgently need financial aid,
I would respectfully solicit instructions as to whether the money de-
posited may be returned prior to the return of the permits. Should the
permits not be returned it is manifest that they may be used by other
persons now domiciled in Central Europe.
Certified true copy
(signature)
pages.zh:
特务科，
1941年1月10日

中欧难民——近期经西伯利亚抵达者
------------------------------------------------------------------

在过去两个月左右的时间里，本办公室注意到，少量中欧犹太难民经西伯利亚和日清汽船株式会社（D.K.K.）从大连的海路抵达上海，但未持有警方签发的移民证书。在某些情况下，资金已由委员会代表这些人存入上海，并由警方签发了许可证。随后许可证被寄往欧洲给相关人员，但在警方注意到的案例中，相关人员在许可证到达欧洲有关城镇之前就已抵达上海。

随后，这些移民在本办公室登记，并自然要求允许他们取走为其存入的资金。由于未能出示证书，他们退还存款的请求遭到拒绝。在每种情况下，移民均被告知，一旦取得证书，将允许他们提取资金。

这种状况显然是由日清汽船株式会社（D.K.K.）对工部局1939年10月22日规章的冷漠态度造成的。轮船公司显然未在发放船票前要求难民出示许可证。在此方面，我还要指出，最近发生了几起难民抵达上海时要么根本没有许可证，要么持有的许可证已过期的情况。无一例外，相关移民均经西伯利亚和日清汽船株式会社（D.K.K.）从大连的海路抵达。

鉴于部分在上海委员会存有资金的移民急需经济援助，本人谨请示是否可在许可证退回之前退还存款。如果许可证未退回，显然它们可能被目前居住在中欧的其他人使用。
核证无误副本
（签名）

December 24, 40.

P. Komor, Esq.,
"I.C." Organization for Immigrants,
Sassoon House,
SHANGHAI.

Sir,

In reply to your letter of December 18, 1940 on
the subject of the issuance of permits for children in
order that they may proceed to Shanghai I have to inform
you that every consideration is given by Shanghai Municipal
Police respecting the issue of such permits, six permits
already having been issued in respect to the children named
on your list.

Residence of the children's parents in the Hongkew
District will not affect the issue of a permit by Shanghai
Municipal Police.

Due to the prevailing political conditions in Europe,
especially France, it is extremely difficult, almost impossible,
to secure a passport to the Far East, therefore I consider
that in the case of parents at present in Shanghai who wish to
evacuate their children from France it would be advisable that
they should first ascertain and make certain that they are
able to arrange for their children to leave France before
making applications to the Shanghai Municipal Police for
permits, for as in the case of the six children for whom
permits have already been issued it is possible that the
period for the validity of these permits will have expired
before the children are due to arrive.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH）

With reference to the attached communication
from the International Committee for the Organization
of European Immigrants in China, I have to point out
that there is no objection from this office to the
issuing of Immigration Certificates for children
now domiciled in Europe to allow them to join their
parents now residing in Shanghai. Six certificates
have already been issued for certain of the children
mentioned in the attached list. Cases of this nature
will always receive sympathetic treatment.

I would like to point out, however, that under
existing conditions in Europe - France especially -
it is almost impossible to secure a passage to the
Far East. Lisbon, in Portugal Spain, is the only port open
for travel to the Far East and it is understood that
the Spanish authorities have placed a quota on the
number of refugees entering Spanish territory for
transhipment to other parts of the world. Transhipment
via the United Kingdom and the United States for
French domiciled refugees is impossible. The only
other way open is via Siberia and refugees in France are
not encouraged to utilize this route which, according
to information received, is extremely expensive.

The parents concerned in Shanghai would be
well advised to make certain that their children are
able to leave France before making their applications
for Immigration Certificates otherwise it is possible

TRANSLATION.

Shanghai, 16th Dec. 1940.

"I. C."

Dear Mr. Komor,

The parents of the children named in the attached list beg to approach the "I.C." with the request to obtain a special immigration permission for their children from the authorities of the International Settlement or French Concession.

The children, mostly under 14 years of age, had been in various Homes in France which had been financed by the Baronesse Rothschild. After the collapse of France, we lived through terrible weeks until we succeeded in obtaining some information on the fate and present residence of our children. It is evident that our children cannot remain any longer in France, where already several institutions have requested other institutions in America to find ways and means of transporting the children to Shanghai, to their parents. A Committee in the U.S.A. is already working in this direction, but its endeavours will be without avail unless the Shanghai authorities permit the children to enter Shanghai.

A few children have Settlement Permits, but most of the parents live in Hongkew, and it is impossible to obtain Permits from the Japanese authorities. The Shanghai Municipal Police has in several cases accepted applications for permits from persons not living in the International Settlement, but in the French Concession. The fact that the parents reside in Hongkew, would, therefore, not speak against the Settlement authorities taking up this special case neglecting the usual procedure. The terrible hardship imposed upon both the children which have been separated from their parents, and the parents themselves should constitute a sufficient reason to give this request the special attention of the authorities concerned, in every way and direction.

The fact that the children reside, at present, in France and that, from the French point of view, it is desirable to remove the children from France, might induce the local French Consul General to issue the permission for the children to enter Shanghai's French Concession.

In any case, we feel that we must apply to these authorities through the intermediary of the "I.C." and that is what prompted us to turn to you with the request to do everything within your power to bring our children back to us. As may be seen from letters, our children have the same desire, i.e. to join their parents again.

Yours faithfully,
(signed:) Dr. Franz Spitzer,
S.R.R.A.Hosp.. No. I,
24o N.-Thibet Road.

上海，1940年12月16日。

“国际委员会”

尊敬的科莫尔先生：

附件名单中所列儿童的父母恳请向“国际委员会”提出请求，希望从公共租界或法租界当局处为其子女获得特别入境许可。

这些儿童大多未满14岁，此前居住在由罗斯柴尔德女男爵（Baronesse Rothschild）资助的法国各收容所中。法国沦陷后，我们度过了可怕的数周，直到成功获悉子女的现状及下落。显然，我们的孩子不能再留在法国，已有几家机构请求美国的其它机构寻找途径和方法，将孩子们运往上海，回到父母身边。美国的一个委员会正为此努力，但若上海当局不允许这些儿童进入上海，其努力将徒劳无功。

少数儿童持有租界居留证，但大多数父母居住在虹口，无法从日本当局获得居留证。上海公共租界工部局警务处在若干案例中已接受并非居住在公共租界、而是居住在法租界的人士提出的居留证申请。因此，父母居住在虹口这一事实，不应成为租界当局忽略常规程序、受理此特殊案例的障碍。骨肉分离的儿童及其父母所遭受的巨大苦难，应足以构成充分理由，促使有关当局在各方面对此请求给予特别关注。

鉴于儿童目前居住在法国，且从法国方面来看，让儿童离开法国是可取的，这可能会促使当地法国总领事签发允许儿童进入上海法租界的许可。

无论如何，我们认为必须通过“国际委员会”作为中介向这些当局提出申请，这也正是我们向您求助的原因，恳请您尽一切可能帮助我们的孩子回到我们身边。从信件中可以看出，我们的孩子也有同样的愿望，即与父母团聚。

此致
敬礼，

N. Y. K. Line
Nippon Yusen Kaisha, 31, the Bund

Shanghai, September 18, 1940.
Ref. P.G.No. 320

The Committee for the Assistance of
European Jewish Refugees in Shanghai,
7, Ave Edward VII.

Attention Mr. Lesser.

Dear Sirs,

Mr. H. Ludolph Hirschfeld.

The above named arrived here on August 4, by our "Asama Maru" from
Kobe as third class passenger without a landing permit.

The Shanghai Municipal Council has taken possession of his passport,
and is now pressing us through the Japanese Consulate-General to send him back
to the port where he embarked by one of our steamers.

Mr. Hirschfeld came from Germany to Japan to leave for Balboa by our
"Rakuyo Maru" and the money for his passage was paid in Germany. The Passage Order
however, was received too late for the sailing of the above vessel from Kobe on
August 2, and in our investigations, it is revealed that as the Japanese transit
visa might expire before the sailing of next steamer for Balboa, the Jewish
Committee in Kobe arranged to send him here without first informing our Kobe
office, who quite erroneously issued a third class ticket to him by our
"Asama Maru".

Our "Yasukuni Maru" is sailing for Balboa from Kobe on October 27,
and we understand that Mr. Hirschfeld will be allowed to land in Kobe by the
Japanese Water-Police if he gets there within ten days of the sailing of the
"Yasukuni Maru" with all the necessary departure.

Thanking for your prompt attention,

We are, Dear Sirs,
yours faithfully,

NIPPON YUSEN KAISHA, Shanghai Branch.

Signature of Sub Manager.

日本邮船株式会社，外滩31号

上海，1940年9月18日。
参考号 P.G.No. 320

致
上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会，
爱德华七世路7号。

注意 莱瑟先生（Mr. Lesser）。

尊敬的先生们：

关于 H. 卢多尔夫·赫希菲尔德先生。

上述人员于8月4日乘坐我社“浅间丸”（Asama Maru）号从神户抵达此处，为三等舱乘客，无登陆许可。

上海公共租界工部局已扣押其护照，现正通过日本总领事馆向我社施压，要求用我社轮船将其送回登船港口。

赫希菲尔德先生从德国来到日本，原计划乘坐我社“鹿野丸”（Rakuyo Maru）号前往巴尔博亚（Balboa），其船费已在德国支付。然而，航行指令收到得太晚，未能赶上上述船只于8月2日从神户启航。经调查得知，由于前往巴尔博亚的下一班船的日本过境签证可能在开船前过期，神户的犹太委员会安排将他送往此处，但未事先通知我社神户办事处，后者错误地为他签发了乘坐我社“浅间丸”号的三等舱船票。

我社“靖国丸”（Yasukuni Maru）号将于10月27日从神户驶往巴尔博亚，据我们了解，如果赫希菲尔德先生能在“靖国丸”号启航前十天内抵达神户，并办妥所有必要的离境手续，日本水上警察将允许其在神户登陆。

感谢贵方的迅速关注，

此致
敬礼，

日本邮船株式会社，上海支店。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
Special Branch - S.l...........Station,
REPORT
Date. September 5, 19 40'

Subject...... Central European Refugees - Rudolph Herbert Israel HIRSCHFEID.

Made by....... D.S.I. Pitts. ......Forwarded by....... D.S.I. Logan.

The contents of the communication
dated August 31, 1940 from Mr. Ishiguro to Mr. Nash
relative to the arrival in Shanghai without entry
permit of R. H. I. HIRSCHFEID have been noted with
interest. This man has paid numerous visits to
this office during the past two weeks for the
purpose of obtaining possession of his passport
and a number of conversations have been held with
him. At no time, however, has he stated that
he has a passage booked on the s.s. Yasukuni Maru
due to leave Kobe on October 28 for Balboa. In
fact he has offered his services to the community
as a police officer, which appears to indicate
that he does not desire to leave Shanghai.

In addition it was observed from his
passport that he holds a visa valid till May 29, 1941
to proceed to Haiti. Asked why he had not continued
his journey to Haiti, Hirschfeld stated that he
preferred to come to Shanghai, where he thought he
had a better chance of earning a livelihood.

If this individual does leave Shanghai
en route to Balboa and Haiti in the near future,
so much the better, but I fail to see how he is to
pay the balance of passage money as mentioned in
the penultimate paragraph of Mr. Ishiguro's letter,
as enquiries reveal he is penniless and is only
living on so-called friends at 27/599 Tongshan Road.

If I may say so, I do not believe he
ever had any intention of proceeding to Haiti.

撰写人....... 副督察长 皮茨（D.S.I. Pitts）。 ......呈送人....... 副督察长 洛根（D.S.I. Logan）。

石黑先生（Mr. Ishiguro）于1940年8月31日致纳什先生（Mr. Nash）关于 R. H. I. 赫希菲尔德无入境许可抵达上海的函件内容已悉，并引起关注。此人在过去两周内多次来访本办公室，目的是取回其护照，并与他进行了多次谈话。然而，他从未声称已预订将于10月28日从神户出发前往巴尔博亚的“靖国丸”号轮船的船位。事实上，他曾主动向社区提供担任警察的服务，这似乎表明他并不希望离开上海。

此外，从其护照中观察到，他持有有效期至1941年5月29日前往海地的签证。当被问及为何未继续前往海地的旅程时，赫希菲尔德表示他更愿意来上海，因为他认为在这里有更好的谋生机会。

如果此人近期确实离开上海，途经巴尔博亚前往海地，那自然是好事，但我看不出他将如何支付石黑先生信件倒数第二段中提到的剩余船费，因为调查显示他身无分文，仅靠居住在通山路599/27号的所谓朋友接济生活。

恕我直言，我不相信他曾经有过前往海地的意图。

Past instances have shown that the possession of
a visa on a German "J" passport to Haiti, for
instance, facilitates the securing of Japanese and
Manchukuo transit visae which are seemingly difficult
for refugees to obtain. The securing of such
transit visae thus makes the passage of the refugee
concerned easier when his final destination is
Shanghai but ostensibly somewhere else.

        Hirschfeld is nothing more nor less
than a young hooligan, whose bona fides are open to
suspicion. His continued presence in Shanghai is
not at all desirable.

K 38/1.
（批：8 SEP 1940 POLICE FORCE）

Japanese Consulate-General,
Shanghai, August 31st, 1940.

Dear Mr. Nash,

With reference to your letter dated August 15th
concerning the arrival here without permit of Rudolph Herbert
Israel Hirschfeld, I write to reply as follows.

According to the report received by the manager of
the local N.Y.K. Office from his colleague at Kobe, the said
party arrived in Kobe from Hamburg, Germany, en route to
Balboa, Panama. However, his passage order per s.s. Rakuyo
Maru of the N.Y.K. Line which was expected to reach Kobe in
time for his departure was overdue. By the time of its arrival,
the term of Hirschfeld's passport visa for transit through
Japan was about to expire. Under the circumstances the said
party approached the N.Y.K. at Kobe through the Jewish Committee
in that port for permitting him to travel by m.v. Asama Maru
to Shanghai.

In the meanwhile the Japanese Authorities allow the
said party to stay in Japan only for 10 days immediately pre-
ceding his departure for Balboa provided that he obtain the
new transit visa from our Consulate-General, the N.Y.K. under-
stand. He has already paid for his passage to Balboa per s.s.
Yasukuni Maru which is due to leave Kobe on October 28th.

Under the circumstances a tentative arrangement is
made between this Consulate-General and the local N.Y.K. office
that the shipping firm will obtain the passage for Hirschfeld on
a boat which will bring him to his destination at the earliest
date, the balance, if any, to be paid by him.

I would like to draw your attention to the fact that
Hirschfeld is now staying in the International Settlement south
of the Soochow Creek. The N.Y.K. is acquainted with his address.

Yours sincerely,

E.T. Nash, Esq.,
Acting Deputy Secretary,
Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

S. Ishiguro,
Consul.

K 38/1.
（批：1940年9月8日 警察部队）

日本驻上海总领事馆，
1940年8月31日，上海。

亲爱的纳什先生：

关于您8月15日来信提及鲁道夫·赫伯特·伊斯雷尔·赫希菲尔德（Rudolph Herbert Israel Hirschfeld）未经许可抵达此处一事，现复函如下。

据本地日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）办事处经理从其神户同事处收到的报告称，该人从德国汉堡抵达神户，途中前往巴拿马巴尔博亚。然而，预计能及时抵达神户供其启程的日本邮船会社“鹿野丸”号（s.s. Rakuyo Maru）轮船延误。待该船抵达时，赫希菲尔德经日本过境的护照签证期限即将届满。在此情况下，该人通过神户的犹太委员会联系日本邮船会社，请求允许其乘坐“浅间丸”号机动船（m.v. Asama Maru）前往上海。

与此同时，日本当局允许该人在日本停留的时间仅限于其前往巴尔博亚出发前的10天，前提是他须从本总领事馆获得新的过境签证，日本邮船会社对此表示理解。他已经支付了乘坐预定于10月28日离开神户的“靖国丸”号（s.s. Yasukuni Maru）前往巴尔博亚的船费。

鉴于上述情况，本总领事馆与本地日本邮船会社办事处达成一项临时安排，即由航运公司为赫希菲尔德预订能使其最早到达目的地的船只舱位，如有差额，由其自行支付。

提请阁下注意，赫希菲尔德目前居住在苏州河以南的国际租界内。日本邮船会社知晓其地址。

此致

敬礼，

E.T. 纳什 先生，
代理副秘书长，
工部局，
上海。

石黑 S.，
领事。

Arriving in Shanghai from Kobe
on August 4, 1940 in the N.Y.K. s.s. Asama Maru
was one Herbert Israel Rudolph HIRSCHFELD. He
is in possession of German Passport J. 13639
issued in Hamburg on July 24, 1939, which states
he was born in Hamburg on January 15, 1921.
HIRSCHFELD claims he is a Jewish
refugee, but despite the fact that he is holding
a German "J" passport, the belief is held that he
is a German Aryan.
At any rate the possession of an
official German "J" passport officially brands him
as a Jew and a refugee. Upon arrival in Shanghai
he was in possession of U.S.$2.00 and ¥15.00. No
permission to land in Shanghai had been given him
by any of the local authorities and accordingly
he was not in possession of a landing permit.
He has no fixed abode and the
Committee rightly refuse to have anything to do
with him since nothing was known of him until his
arrival here.

N.Y.K. Line - is responsible for verifying that a
permit has been issued by the Police before a passage
booking is made. In this instance this rule does
not appear to have been fulfilled. HIRSCHFELD'S
passport is being held by this office until such

CONFIDENTIAL

May 27, 40.

Central European Jews - French Police stop issuing immigration
Permits.

In accordance with instructions received
from the French Consulate-General, the French
Police have ceased issuing immigration permits
allowing European Jewish refugees to enter
the French Concession.

This move was brought about by reason of
the fact that far too many refugees are now residing
in the French Concession which from an accommodation
standpoint is practically fully occupied.

In addition it would appear that the
French authorities are now exercising their
powers to prevent any "fifth column" activities
in the Concession that might be caused by the
further influx of refugees, regarding many of
whom details are difficult to secure until after
their arrival here since they land in possession
of U.S.$400, which permits free entry into the
Settlement (South of the Creek) and virtually
into the French Concession.

根据从法国总领事馆收到的指示，法国警察已停止签发允许欧洲犹太难民进入法租界的移民许可证。

此举是由于目前居住在法租界的难民过多，从住宿角度来看，法租界实际上已完全满员。

此外，法国当局似乎正在行使其权力，以防止因难民进一步涌入而在租界内可能引发的任何“第五纵队”活动，鉴于许多难民的详细情况在他们抵达此地之前难以获取，因为他们登陆时持有400美元，这允许他们自由进入租界（苏州河以南）并实际上进入法租界。

Further to a report submitted by this
office on May 2, 1940 I have to state that in the
s.s. "Conte Rosso", ex-Europe, arriving in Shanghai

Triestino offices in Europe.

The above details fully confirm the
anticipations voiced in the report of May 2, 1940
and since many of these arrivals, after examination,
appear to be far from respectable types, the atten-
tion of the Council is again drawn to the fact that
Shanghai would benefit considerably if Article (1)
of the Regulations were amended to exclude refugees
depositing landing money in Europe against their
arrival here. If the money were deposited in
Shanghai in the first instance, we would be better
enabled to judge the merits of each individual case.

26 APR 1940
POLICE FORCE

COMMITTEE FOR THE ASSISTANCE OF EUROPEAN JEWISH REFUGEES
IN SHANGHAI

IMMIGRATION DEPARTMENT

Embankment Building,
Shanghai, April 25, 1940.

E.T. Nash, Esq.,
Assistant Secretary,
S.M.C.

Dear Mr. Nash,

Re Richard I. Grunwald:

Referring to your inquiry over the phone and your memo of date I wish to say that, in my endeavour not to do injustice to the party referred to, I have made investigations regarding the affair, have obtained a verbal explanation from Grunwald and hold his written statement in the German language.

According to Grunwald's assertions an amount of U.S.$690 was placed at the disposal of his wife by relatives in Sydney and New York. Of this sum $290 was to serve as travelling expenses and $400 as landing money here.

Grunwald himself was held in prison in Austria, but pardoned on condition that he emigrates at once. Thereupon his wife ceded her rights to the said deposit with the Lloyd Triestino to her husband. But the Lloyd Triestino retained the balance of U.S.$400 there, an assertion which I have no means of verifying.

In his written statement Grunwald maintains that the Special Branch of the S. M. Police took his travelling ticket and his passport and is still holding both. He also states that on the ticket a remark can be found, according to which the $400 needed upon landing in Shanghai, was on deposit with the head office of the Lloyd Triestino.

Since the ticket is supposed to be in the hands of the police, I think it would be simple to ascertain whether or not such a remark is to be found on the ticket. In the affirmative one ought not to doubt the bona fides of Grunwald. The latter declared in writing that the Lloyd in Trieste had told him that he could safely proceed to Shanghai.

Now as to remedial measures I should like to suggest the following:

(a) Find out from Mr. Pitts whether or not the ticket of Grunwald bears a remark as to the existence of U.S.$400 as landing money.

(b) If yes, the money ought to be remitted here by cable at the expense of the Lloyd, who knows the regulations.

(c) Possibly it might have been intended to use the money bringing out his wife; on this point I have no reliable information. In this case (although not in the spirit of the regulations) I should suggest to permit ( as an exception).

亲爱的 Nash 先生：

关于 Richard I. Grunwald：

参照阁下的电话查询及备忘录，我愿说明，为了不对所述当事人造成不公，我已对此事进行调查，从 Grunwald 处获得了口头解释，并持有其德文书面陈述。

根据 Grunwald 的说法，其在悉尼和纽约的亲属将其妻子名下的一笔 690 美元款项交由其支配。其中 290 美元用作旅费，400 美元作为在此地的登陆费。

Grunwald 本人曾在奥地利被监禁，但以立即离境为条件获得赦免。随后，其妻子将在意大利邮船公司（Lloyd Triestino）的上述存款权益转让给了丈夫。但意大利邮船公司保留了剩余的 400 美元，这一说法我无从核实。

在其书面陈述中，Grunwald 声称上海公共租界警务处特别处拿走了他的船票和护照，并至今仍扣留两者。他还声称，船票上有一处备注，注明在上海登陆所需的 400 美元已存入意大利邮船公司总部。

既然船票据称在警方手中，我认为核实船票上是否有此类备注应该很简单。如果有，就不应怀疑 Grunwald 的诚意。后者书面声明，里雅斯特的意大利邮船公司告诉他可以安全前往上海。

至于补救措施，我建议如下：

(a) 向 Pitts 先生查明 Grunwald 的船票上是否有关于 400 美元登陆费存在的备注。

(b) 如果有，这笔钱应由知晓规章的意大利邮船公司自费通过电汇汇至此处。

(c) 也许原本打算用这笔钱接出其妻子；对此点我没有可靠信息。在这种情况下（虽然不符合规章精神），我建议作为例外允许

pages.en:
2.

the arrival of Mrs. Grunwald in Shanghai, for with U.S.$400
both can start anew in life here.

(d) Ask the Lloyd Triestino for a written explanation of the case,
and if found unsatisfactory, point to the obligation of the
steamship company to transport Grunwald back to Italy.

I should like to reiterate my verbal statement that my
Committee would not object to place Grunwald in one of our Homes
in Hongkew, until he can obtain funds from relatives in America.
But the Japanese authorities will not permit this. On the other
hand, we have no sufficient means to care for his maintenance in
the Settlement.

According to the emphatic assertions of Grunwald he has
acted bona fide, for (as he says) the funds were there when
leaving, and he had the assurance of the Lloyd in Trieste that
everything was alright. I hold the copy of a document from the
public prosecutor in Austria, stating that Grunwald was liberated
on certain conditions, one of which stipulates that he must not
return again. If he does it means hell in the fullest sense of
the word. As a foretaste they have already knocked out his front
teeth.

So here we have a tragic case, possibly not entirely the
fault of Grunwald. There will be no return steamer to Trieste
until earliest May 12, so that there remains time to sympathetically
consider the case and investigate its merits.

Needless to say, I shall continue to remain at your disposal
for further investigation and information.

With compliments I beg to remain,

Very truly Yours,

E. Kann.
pages.zh:
2.

Grunwald 夫人抵达上海，因为有了这 400 美元，两人都可以在此重新开始生活。

(d) 要求意大利邮船公司就此案作出书面解释，如果解释不能令人满意，则指出轮船公司有义务将 Grunwald 运回意大利。

我想重申我的口头声明，即我的委员会不反对将 Grunwald 安置我们在虹口的一处收容所中，直到他能从美国的亲属处获得资金。但日本当局不允许这样做。另一方面，我们没有足够的 средств 来负担他在租界的生活费用。

根据 Grunwald 的坚决主张，他是出于诚意行事的，因为（正如他所说）离开时资金是到位的，而且他得到了里雅斯特意大利邮船公司的保证，一切正常。我持有一份奥地利公诉人的文件副本， stating 指出 Grunwald 是在某些条件下获释的，其中一条规定他不得再次返回。如果他回去，那将意味着陷入地狱般的境地。作为预兆，他们已经打掉了他的门牙。

因此，这是一个悲剧性的案例，可能并不完全是 Grunwald 的错。最早也要到 5 月 12 日才有返回里雅斯特的轮船，因此还有时间同情地考虑此案并调查其是非曲直。

不用说，我将随时听候阁下进一步调查和提供信息。

顺致敬意，

您真诚的，

E. Kann.

Gentlemen,

It has been reported to the Council by the Commissioner
of Police that your Company permitted the embarkation on the s.s.
"Conte Verde", which arrived here on April 4, of a refugee by the
name of R. I. Gruenwald, notwithstanding that he had failed to
comply with the regulations governing the entry of European
refugees into Shanghai.

I have to request a full explanation of the action of
your Company in permitting a breach of the regulations, in order
that the Council may consider whether or not it should require the
return of the refugee in question to the port of embarkation.

I am, Gentlemen,
Your obedient Servant,

G. Godfrey Phillips

Messrs. Lloyd Triestino,

Gentlemen,

The Police Department has drawn attention to the serious lack of co-operation and organization displayed by the officers of the S. S. "CONTE ROSSO" in connection with the disembarkation of Jewish refugees from Europe arriving in this steamer on March 8.

The efforts of the Jewish Committee and of the Police Department were considerably hampered by the absence of any means to distinguish between the refugees and other passengers. No separate and detailed lists of the Jewish refugee arrivals were available for this purpose, and the passports of the refugees had not been collected by the ship's officers.

In inviting your co-operation to prevent the recurrence of the difficulties experienced by the Police on this occasion, I have to request that you will be so good as to devise a procedure to govern the future disembarkation of Jewish refugees which is satisfactory to the Special Branch of the Police Department.

I am, Gentlemen,
Your obedient Servant,

During the morning and afternoon of March 8,
1940, Mr. E. VALENTINI of the Lloyd Triestino Line,
telephoned this office and intimated that one
GRUENWALD, an emigrant from Germany, was arriving in
the s.s. "Conte Rosso" between 5 p.m. and 6 p.m. the
same day. He was in possession of neither a landing
permit nor the requisite U.S. $400, stated Mr. VALENTINI,
who asked whether arrangements could be made to allow
him to disembark despite the fact that such a procedure
was not in accordance with the existing regulations
relating to immigration.

These facts were immediately placed before the
D.C. (Special Branch) who just as quickly passed them
to Mr. E. T. NASH, Assistant Secretary, Shanghai
Municipal Council. Instructions were finally given
that since no local Jewish Committee would undertake
the responsibility of supporting GRUENWALD he was not
to be allowed ashore and was to leave Shanghai in the
same steamer as he arrived.

At 5.30 p.m. D.S. Pitts proceeded to the Shanghai
& Hongkew Wharf and there met Mr. VALENTINI. These
two persons went on board the "Conte Rosso" and the
captain was immediately asked to produce the person
of GRUENWALD. The captain replied that no such
person was on his ship whereupon Mr. VALENTINI
explained that Lloyd Triestino in Trieste had wired
him earlier that day that a mistake had been made in
issuing GRUENWALD a ticket. The captain still maintained

1940年3月8日上午及下午，意大利劳埃德三隅航运公司的 E. VALENTINI 先生致电本办公室，
告知一名来自德国的移民 GRUENWALD 将于当日下午5点至6点之间乘坐“孔特·罗索”号（Conte Rosso）轮船抵达。
VALENTINI 先生称，该人既无登陆许可证，也未持有规定的400美元，
并询问是否可以安排其上岸，尽管此举不符合现行的移民法规。

这些情况立即呈报给副总监（特别科），后者随即迅速将其转呈给上海公共租界工部局助理秘书 E. T. NASH 先生。
最终下达的指示是，由于没有本地犹太委员会愿意承担资助 GRUENWALD 的责任，
故不准其上岸，并要求其乘坐原船离开上海。

下午5时30分，D.S. Pitts 前往上海与虹口码头，并在那里会见了 VALENTINI 先生。
两人登上“孔特·罗索”号，并立即要求船长交出 GRUENWALD。
船长回答说船上没有此人，随后 VALENTINI 先生解释说，
意大利劳埃德三隅航运公司特里亚斯特总部当天早些时候曾发电报给他，
称向 GRUENWALD 签发船票是一个错误。船长仍坚持

May 15, 40.

S. Ishiguro, Esq.,
H. I. J. M. Consulate General,
Shanghai.

Dear Mr. Ishiguro,

You will remember that at the time we reached an agreement as to the regulations governing the entry of European Refugees into Shanghai, it was suggested that from time to time we might exchange particulars as to the number of entries permitted by our two Authorities under the regulations. Accordingly, for your information I have to inform you that the number arriving by virtue of monetary qualifications is 439, and the number of valid permits issued up to May 15 is 812 covering 1213 persons. Of the 1213 persons entitled to enter under permit, only 240 have arrived. The total of arrivals under the regulations up to May 15 is therefore 679.

In requesting that we may be favoured with particulars of the entries permitted North of the Creek under the regulations, I have to allude to references in the local refugee newspapers to the possible issue by your Consulate-General of a very considerable number of entry permits.

In order that some measure of correspondence may be maintained in the effective application of the regulations governing entry of refugees North and South of the Creek, I should be very grateful if we may be informed (1) as to the number of permits issued by your Consulate-General under the regulations and the number of persons covered, (2) as to the present provisions of your regulations governing entry of refugees North of the Creek, and (3) as to whether you are still maintaining the original requirement that the economic sufficiency of new entrants or their local relatives should be ensured by investigation thereinto by the Refugee Committee.

Thanking you for your continued kind co-operation in this matter.

Yours sincerely,

E. T. MANN
Assistant Secretary.

COMMITTEE FOR THE ASSISTANCE OF EUROPEAN JEWISH REFUGEES IN SHANGHAI

25th April 1940

COPY.

S. Ishiguro, Esq.,
Consul for Japan,
Shanghai.

Dear Mr. Ishiguro,

Re: Immigration

From the "8-Uhr Abendblatt", an emigrant evening paper, of April 23, I learn that 1,000 immigration permits for Hongkew residence are about to be issued. The issue of 20th April of the same paper contains a notice, telling applicants when to apply (according to the alphabet) to the Japanese Consulate General for delivery of the landing permits already referred to. All these applications were submitted without the intermediary of our Committee, so that the latter was not enabled to investigate the bona fides of the applicants; nor could we examine the prospects of the new arrivals to make a living in Shanghai.

While welcoming the idea to help people to get out from Central Europe and enable them to start life afresh in a new land, we feel apprehensive as to the ability of the newcomers to stand on their own feet. Since November last year, when immigration was again permitted under certain restrictions, our Committee has carefully examined the statements made in writing by applicants and has invariably passed on such requests only, which contained a fair chance that the newcomers will not become a burden to either our Committee, or to the Shanghai community at large.

Recently the Electioneering Association, consisting of re□ a body without juridical standing□ has inaugurated a campaign for the issue of immigration permits. We have no desire whatsoever to either criticise, nor to interfere in any way with the decisions your Consulate General in this respect. On the contrary, we really remain thankful for the great kindness you have displayed towards unfortunate masses of citizens who are forced to abandon their ho□ But on the other hand, I feel dutibound to place on record that:

(a) our Committee cannot accept responsibility for the bo□ fides of both the applicants and the immigrants, as long as the applications have not been passing through our hands for examina□ of the statements contained therein.

-2-
pages.zh:
上海援助欧洲犹太难民委员会

1940年4月25日

副本。

S. Ishiguro 先生，
日本领事，
上海。

亲爱的 Ishiguro 先生：

事由：移民

我从4月23日的移民晚报《八点钟晚报》（8-Uhr Abendblatt）中获悉，
即将签发1,000份虹口居住区的移民许可证。
同一报纸4月20日的版面包含一则通知，告知申请人何时按字母顺序
向日本总领事馆申请领取前述的登陆许可证。
所有这些申请均未通过本委员会中介提交，
因此本委员会无法调查申请人的真实性；
我们也无法审查新来者在上海谋生的前景。

虽然我们对帮助人们离开中欧并使他们在新土地上重新开始生活的想法表示欢迎，
但我们对新来者自立的能力感到担忧。
自去年11月移民在一定限制下再次获准以来，
本委员会仔细审查了申请人提交的书面陈述，
并且仅转呈那些新来者不太可能成为本委员会或整个上海社区负担的申请。

最近，一个由 re□ 组成的缺乏法律地位的团体 □ 发起了一场争取签发移民许可证的运动。
我们绝无意批评或以任何方式干涉贵总领事馆在此方面的决定。
相反，我们确实对您向被迫放弃家园的不幸民众所表现出的巨大善意表示感谢。
但另一方面，我觉得有责任记录在案：

(a) 只要申请未经过本委员会审查其中包含的陈述，
本委员会就不能接受对申请人和移民真实性的责任。

-2-

pages.en:
COMMITTEE FOR THE ASSISTANCE OF EUROPEAN JEWISH REFUGEES IN SHANGHAI

- 2 -

(b) that, in the event of emigrants arriving here without
means - especially if this happens in large numbers - our Committee
will most likely be unable to take them to the Homes, and maintain
them there for a lengthy period of time.

Bringing to your notice for your kind consideration the
contents of this last paragraph is really the main purpose of this
letter. The means at our disposal are dwindling as time goes on
and I fear that we should not be able to cope with the requirements
of a large mass of people landing here without means and being
unable to care for their own support.

This does not mean that our Committee does not want to see
an increase in the size of the refugee population here. As a matter
of fact, we at all times welcome the growth of the emigrants colony
in China and shall gladly place our advice and assistance at its
disposal. But what circumstances demand is that newcomers ought to
be able to stand on their own feed ant not be dependent upon the very
slender monetary resources of our Committee.

I thought it advisable to bring to your kind notice these
actualities and desire to thank you once more for the very helpful
consideration which you hitherto have been good enough to devote to
a really worthy cause.

Believe me, dear Mr. Ishiguro,

Very sincerely yours,

signed: E. Kann
pages.zh:
上海援助欧洲犹太难民委员会

- 2 -

(b) 如果移民身无分文地抵达这里——尤其是如果这种情况大量发生——
本委员会很可能无法将他们安置到收容所，并长期维持他们的生活。

提请阁下善意考虑最后一段的内容确实是这封信的主要目的。
随着时间的推移，我们要支配的资金日益减少，
我担心我们将无法应对大量身无分文、无法自给自足的人登陆这里的需求。

这并不意味着本委员会不希望看到此地难民人口规模的增加。
事实上，我们随时欢迎在华移民群体的增长，
并乐意提供我们的建议和援助。
但形势要求新来者应当能够自立，
而不依赖本委员会非常有限的资金资源。

我认为将这些实际情况提请阁下注意是明智之举，
并再次感谢您迄今为止对这一真正有价值的事业所给予的非常有益的关注。

相信您，亲爱的 Ishiguro 先生，

您真诚的，

签名: E. Kann

Gentlemen,

I have to refer to your letter of September 6,
addressed to the Commissioner of Police, enquiring as
to the definition of the term European Refugee for the
purposes of enforcement of the Council's regulations of
June 1, 1940, copy of which I enclose, relating to the
entry of European Refugees into the International Settlement of Shanghai South of the Soochow Creek.

I have to inform you that the regulations in
question are designed to prevent the entry into the
Settlement of all destitutes, including refugees who
were emigrating from Europe in large numbers.

In practice the application of these regulations to persons wishing to travel to Shanghai has been
left to the Shipping Companies at Ports of proposed
departure. No exact definition of the term has
previously been asked for by the Shipping Companies.

All National Authorities and Shipping Companies
have willingly co-operated to ensure that the Council's
regulations shall achieve the end designed, namely to
prevent European destitutes of any nationality whatever
from entering the Settlement and becoming a burden upon
local charity.

I am, Gentlemen,
Your obedient Servant,

E. T. NASH

Acting Deputy Secretary.

诸位先生：

兹提及你们9月6日致警务处处长的信函，询问为了执行工部局1940年6月1日关于欧洲难民进入苏州河以南上海公共租界的规定（副本随附），对“欧洲难民”一词的定义。

我必须通知你们，有关规定的目的是防止所有赤贫者，包括大量从欧洲移民出来的难民，进入租界。

在实际操作中，这些规定适用于希望前往上海的人员，其执行工作已留给拟出发港口的轮船公司。此前，轮船公司从未要求对该术语进行确切定义。

各国当局和轮船公司均自愿合作，以确保工部局的规定达到预期目的，即防止任何国籍的欧洲赤贫者进入租界并成为当地慈善事业的负担。

此致，
敬礼

你们的恭顺仆人，

E. T. NASH

代理副秘书长。

Special Branch - S.1.
September 26, 1940.

Central European Refugees - Communication from P. & O. Line.

The expression "European Refugees"
as mentioned in the attached communication and enclosure
is, however one looks at it, a term of considerable
elasticity. When the Municipal Council framed
the regulations relating to the immigration into
Shanghai of "European refugees," it did so for the
purpose of preventing unhindered ingress into Shanghai
of Europeans rendered destitute through the machinations
of militarists dominating the Central European stage.
This applied particularly and practically to Europeans
of Jewish faith who had been stripped of their wealth
and belongings following the incidence of certain anti-
Semitic decrees in areas occupied by the above mentioned
factions.

The Municipal regulations were
put into effect in October 1939 when Shanghai was
gradually being inundated by the unrestricted influx
of German and Austrian Jews, many of whom on arrival
here, were penniless and forced to become inmates of
refugee camps in order to exist. As a result of the
effect these unfortunates were having on the local
economic structure, the regulations were enforced for
the primary purpose of ensuring that no further
destitute Central European (e.g. German, Austrian,
Czech, Polish, Danzig, etc.) Jews were allowed to
enter Shanghai.

The regulations did not and do not
apply to non-Jewish nationals of the countries mentioned
higher. above
pages.zh:
政治部 - S.1.
1940年9月26日。

中欧难民 - 来自半岛与东方轮船公司 (P. & O. Line) 的公函。

然而，无论怎么看，附件公函及附文中提到的“欧洲难民”一词都具有相当大的弹性。当工部局制定关于“欧洲难民”移居上海的规章时，其目的是防止因主宰中欧舞台的军国主义者的阴谋而陷入赤贫的欧洲人不受阻碍地进入上海。这特别且实际地适用于犹太教欧洲人，他们在上述派系占领的地区因某些反犹法令的实施而被剥夺了财富和财产。

工部局规章于1939年10月生效，当时上海正逐渐被德国和奥地利犹太人的 unrestricted influx（无限制涌入）所淹没，其中许多人抵达这里时身无分文，为了生存被迫成为难民营的收容人员。由于这些不幸者对当地经济结构产生的影响，执行这些规定的主要目的是确保不再允许更多赤贫的中欧（例如德国、奥地利、捷克、波兰、但泽等）犹太人进入上海。

上述国家的非犹太籍国民过去和现在均不适用这些规定。

pages.en:
- 2 -

In practice, therefore, the expression
"European refugees" as interpreted by this office in
the light of the Regulations, can be summed up as :-

"Persons of Jewish faith or race resident in
a Central European Country or area, desirous
of settling down in Shanghai in order to
escape political oppression resulting from
their religious beliefs."

Certified true copy

J. Fancello
CSC
pages.zh:
- 2 -

因此，在实践中，本部门根据规章解释的“欧洲难民”一词可以概括为：

“居住在中欧国家或地区，为了逃避因其宗教信仰而产生的政治压迫，希望在上海定居的犹太教信仰或犹太种族人士。”

经核证无误副本

J. Fancello
CSC

Special Branch.
August 6, 1941.

Central European Refugees.- Proposed
Expulsion from the Hongkew Area of
Certain Jewish refugees.
----------------------------------------

With reference to the contents of the attached
article appearing in the North-China Daily News
of August 6, 1941, enquiries reveal that the
Japanese authorities do not yet contemplate
taking action as indicated in the initial paragraph
of the article, the matter at the moment merely
being "Under consideration." In this connection
your attention is drawn to a report submitted by
this office on July 14, 1941 under the heading
of "CENTRAL EUROPEAN REFUGEES - Registration of
Jewish Refugees in Hongkew area."

It is a fact that the majority of refugee
criminals are residents of the Hongkew area but
their crimes have invariably been petty ones whilst
taking into consideration the Jewish refugee
population in Shanghai the number of criminals
is an extremely small one. What is exactly meant
by the Japanese authorities when they refer to
"undesirable elements" is not quite clear since
they themselves have been responsible for allowing
numerous immigrants to enter Shanghai and Hongkew
without first being in possession of the necessary
immigration permits. (See report of July 14, 1941).

The article refers to an interview given the
newspaper by a refugee named SOMMER who is described
as "a prominent refugee resident of Shanghai."
SOMMER likes to think himself prominent but in actual
pages.zh:
特别处。
1941年8月6日。

中欧难民。- 拟将部分犹太难民从虹口地区驱逐出境。
----------------------------------------

关于附上的刊登于1941年8月6日《字林西报》的文章内容，经查询显示，日本当局尚未考虑采取文章首段所述之行动，目前此事仅处于“审议中”。就此而言，提请阁下注意本办公室于1941年7月14日提交的题为“中欧难民 - 虹口地区犹太难民登记”的报告。

Expulsion of Certain Jews
From Hongkew Proposed

THE expulsion of a certain percentage of the Jewish refugee community in Japanese-controlled areas is being seriously studied at the present moment, stated Commander N. Hazama, the Navy spokesman, at the Japanese press conference yesterday. As a result of these investigations, he continued it is probable that some of the more undesirable characters will be expelled, although it is as yet uncertain when this will take place.

The underlying motive of this new step on the part of the Japanese authorities, Commander Hazama explained, was connected with the desire for the stabilization of living conditions in the Jewish refugee colony north of the Creek. It appears that quite a number of the refugees, mostly comprised of the undesirable element, entered Hongkew without the necessary permits and are said to be affecting the rentals and food-prices in the Jewish area. Fearing that discontent on the part of the lawful residents may lead to active disturbances between the two factors, thus further detracting from the peace and order of the Hongkew area, the Japanese authorities are seeking to preserve the welfare of the Jewish refugees by removing all undesirable characters, the Navy spokesman asserted.

No Measure of Force

He further stressed the fact that no measure of force will accompany the expulsions. "These will be carried out only through the initiative of the Jewish Residents Association," he stated.

Questioned as to where the undesirables will go after they have been expelled from Japanese-controlled areas, Commander Hazama replied that this point had not as yet been considered by the authorities.

Protest Delivered

News of impending Japanese action to weed out "undesirables" among the Jewish refugee community in Hongkew and Wayside has caused considerable alarm in that community, according to Mr. L. Sommer, editor of the "Far Eastern Commercial Telegraph" and a prominent refugee resident in Shanghai, who yesterday delivered a written protest to the Japanese authorities against the proposed action.

In an interview with a representative of the "North-China Daily News," Mr. Sommer pointed out that the proposed Japanese step had been foreshadowed by an article that had appeared in the "Shanghai Jewish Chronicle," in which it was stated that officials of the Japanese Naval Landing Party had invited some members of the Jewish refugee community, including Messrs. O. Levine, editor of the "Shanghai Jewish Chronicle," Mr. Weinberger, dismissed refugee camp chief, Wachner, Dr. Kardegt and Dr. Lessner, to act as a sub-committee to work with the Japanese Naval Landing Party in weeding out "undesirables."

In the article, Mr. Sommer went on, it was pointed out that Jewish refugees without permits to live in Hongkew would be deported immediately after investigations by the sub-committee, which would also report to the Japanese Naval Landing Party as to whether or not certain Jewish refugees were desirable.

S.M.C. Not Consulted

According to Mr. Sommer, who stated that he spoke on behalf of twelve to thirteen thousand Jewish and other refugees in Hongkew, the men who had been approached by the Japanese to form a sub-committee were not entitled to represent the whole of the Hongkew refugee community. Most of them, he said, did not reside in Hongkew and, he added, they had not consulted other Jewish leaders.

Furthermore, the proposed Japanese action was illegal, Mr. Sommer stated, as there had been no approaches to the Shanghai Municipal Council—Hongkew being part of the International Settlement—nor had any appointed Jewish body in Shanghai been approached on the proposed Japanese action.

Mr. Sommer added that he felt such unilateral if carried out, would tend to increase tension in Shanghai.

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
AUG 8 1941.

拟驱逐部分犹太人

日本海军发言人间岛（N. Hazama）指挥官在昨日的日本记者招待会上称，目前正认真研究驱逐日控区内一定比例的犹太难民。他接着说，根据这些调查结果，可能会驱逐一些较为不良分子，尽管何时执行尚不确定。

间岛指挥官解释说，日本当局采取这一新举措的根本动机，与希望稳定苏州河以北犹太难民聚居区的生活状况有关。看来，相当数量的难民（主要由不良分子组成）在没有必要许可证的情况下进入虹口，据说影响了犹太区的租金和食品价格。海军发言人声称，日本当局担心合法居民的不满可能导致两方之间发生主动骚乱，从而进一步损害虹口地区的和平与秩序，因此试图通过清除所有不良分子来维护犹太难民的福祉。

不使用武力

他进一步强调，驱逐行动不会伴随任何强制措施。“这些行动将仅通过犹太居民协会的倡议来执行，”他说。

当被问及不良分子被逐出日控区后将去向何处时，间岛指挥官回答说，当局尚未考虑这一点。

递交抗议

据《远东商业电讯报》编辑、上海著名难民居民 L. Sommer 先生称，关于日本即将在虹口及越界筑路区（Wayside）的犹太难民社区中清除“不良分子”的消息，在该社区引起了相当大的恐慌。Sommer 先生昨日向日本当局递交了一份书面抗议，反对拟议中的行动。

在接受《字林西报》代表采访时，Sommer 先生指出，日本拟议中的这一步骤已在《上海犹太纪事报》刊登的一篇文章中有所预示。该文章称，日本海军陆战队官员邀请了一些犹太难民社区的成员，包括《上海犹太纪事报》编辑 O. Levine 先生、被免职的难民营主管 Weinberger 先生、Wachner、Kardegt 博士和 Lessner 博士，组成一个小组委员会，与日本海军陆战队合作清除“不良分子”。

Sommer 先生继续说，文章中指出，没有居住在虹口许可证的犹太难民将在小组委员会调查后立即被驱逐，该委员会还将向日本海军陆战队报告某些犹太难民是否属于受欢迎之列。

未咨询工部局

据 Sommer 先生称，他表示自己代表虹口的一万二千至一万三千名犹太及其他难民发言，那些被日本人接触以组成小组委员会的人无权代表整个虹口难民社区。他说，他们大多数人并不居住在虹口，并补充说，他们也没有与其他犹太领袖协商。

此外，Sommer 先生表示，日本拟议中的行动是非法的，因为并未接洽上海公共租界工部局——虹口是公共租界的一部分——也没有就日本拟议的行动接洽上海任何指定的犹太机构。

Sommer 先生补充说，他觉得如果这种单边行动得以实施，将会加剧上海的紧张局势。

《字林西报》
1941年8月8日。

SHANGHAI TIMES,
AUG 6 1941.

Undesirable
Refugees To
Be Expelled

Nippon Navy Spokesman
Says Investigations
Now Proceeding

Undesirable Jewish elements now residing in Japanese-occupied territory will be expelled after due investigations have been concluded, Commander Hazama, the Japanese Navy spokesman, revealed yesterday afternoon at the regular weekly press conference. Expulsion will be made regardless of whether the Jews concerned hold permits of entry or not, he explained.

When asked as to how the measure will be carried out, the spokesman pointed out that it will depend upon the discretion of the Jewish Refugee Residents Association with which the Japanese authorities are understood to be negotiating on the matter.

Commander Hazama said that the increase in rents and cost of commodities in the Wayside and Hongkew areas are partly due to the influx of Jews who had not obtained any permits from the proper authorities. The presence of undesirable elements in the district affects peace and order in the community, he declared, adding that their expulsion would be beneficial to the Jewish community as a whole.

The spokesman also stated that each individual case is being treated separately in the course of investigations now underway. Asked as to when the expulsions would begin he answered that it would entirely depend upon the results of the inquiry and the action to be taken by the Jewish Refugee Residents Association.

不良
难民将
被驱逐

日本海军发言人
称调查
正在进行中

日本海军发言人间岛指挥官昨天下午在例行每周记者招待会上透露，现居日军占领区的不良犹太分子在完成适当调查后将被驱逐。他解释说，无论相关犹太人是否持有入境许可证，都将予以驱逐。

当被问及该措施将如何执行时，发言人指出，这将取决于犹太难民居民协会的决定，据悉日本当局正就此事项与该协会进行谈判。

间岛指挥官说，越界筑路区和虹口地区租金及商品成本的增加，部分是由于没有从适当当局获得许可证的犹太人涌入所致。他宣称，该地区存在不良分子会影响社区的和平与秩序，并补充说，驱逐他们将有利于整个犹太社区。

发言人还表示，在目前正在进行的调查中，每个案件都在单独处理。当被问及驱逐何时开始时，他回答说，这完全取决于调查结果以及犹太难民居民协会将采取的行动。

Special Branch,
July 14, 1941.

CENTRAL EUROPEAN REFUGEES - Registration
of Jewish Refugees in Hongkew area.

With reference to the contents of the attached
report which appeared in all local foreign newspapers
the Japanese Naval Landing Party is, as stated,
making a periodical registration of refugees residing
in Hongkew. As far as can be seen this registration
affects this office in two ways only, viz:

1) There are and have been a number of refugees who
have entered Shanghai by virtue of a Settlement
Immigration Certificate. They have all been
warned that they must reside in the Settlement,
South of Soochow Creek, but it has been observed
on occasions that after a short period of residence
South of the Creek they go North of the Creek to
take up their domicile. As far as possible, we
have instructed these persons to leave Hongkew
for abodes South of the Creek and generally our
instructions have been complied with. We have
no power, however, to make them remove from North
to South of the Creek.

2) As mentioned many times previously certain Japanese
shipping concerns have transported to Shanghai
refugees without permits. The majority of these
refugees are residing North of the Creek and the
stand is maintained that since they arrived here
without permission from the Council they should
be the worry of the Japanese authorities.

Refugees, apart from those at present in
Vladivostock or Japan en route to Shanghai, can now
only travel to Shanghai via Portugal or Marseilles.

Certified true copy.

政治部，
1941年7月14日。

中欧难民 - 虹口地区犹太难民登记。

鉴于所附报告中提及的内容已刊登于所有本地外文报纸，正如所述，日本海军陆战队正在对居住在虹口的难民进行定期登记。就目前看来，此次登记仅在以下两个方面影响本办公室：

1) 过去和现在都有一些难民凭借公共租界移民证书进入上海。他们都曾受到警告，必须居住在苏州河以南的公共租界内，但有时观察到，他们在苏州河以南短暂居住一段时间后，便前往河北岸定居。我们已尽可能指示这些人离开虹口，前往苏州河以南的住所，通常我们的指示都得到了遵守。然而，我们无权强制他们从河北岸迁往河南岸。

2) 如前多次提及，某些日本航运公司将无许可证的难民运至上海。这些难民大多居住在河北岸，我方坚持认为，既然他们未经工部局许可抵达此地，他们应成为日本当局关注的问题。

除了目前位于符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）或日本、正在前往上海途中的难民外，现在的难民只能通过葡萄牙或马赛前往上海。

认证真实副本。

REGISTRATION OF JEWISH REFUGEES
IN HONGKEW.

Yesterday it was announced by representatives of
the Japanese authorities that all Jewish refugees residing
in Hongkew and Wayside districts must register with the Ja-
panese authorities.

The registration will be carried out in order to
establish the identity of each person residing in the said
districts, a special attention being paid to the question as
to criminal antecedents any of the refugees may possibly
have. Besides, the registration will show if all Jewish
refugees residing in Wayside and Hongkew districts had the
necessary permits to enter Shanghai.

It is expected that the regulations governing the
admission of Jewish refugees in our port will be revised in
the near future.

Certified true copy.

1941年6月4日俄文报纸《言论报》（SLOVO）刊登文章的译文。由 I.M. Altadukoff 先生编辑出版，地址：阿尔伯特王路238号

虹口犹太难民
登记。

昨日，日本当局代表宣布，所有居住在虹口和越界筑路区的犹太难民必须向日本当局登记。

进行登记是为了确定居住在上述地区的每个人的身份，特别关注难民可能拥有的犯罪前科问题。此外，登记还将显示居住在越界筑路区和虹口区的所有犹太难民是否拥有进入上海的必要许可证。

预计不久后将修订管辖犹太难民进入我国港口的规定。

认证真实副本。

K 38/1
POLICE FORCE
FOR INFORMATION
SEP. 194T
COMMITTEE FOR THE ASSISTANCE OF EUROPEAN JEWISH REFUGEES
IN SHANGHAI
7 Avenue Edward VII
Shanghai, September 4, 1941
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REGISTRY
8422(C)
G. Godfrey Phillips, Esq.,
Secretary & Commissioner General,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

On Friday afternoon, the 30th of August, a
cablegram reached me from the Jewish Community at Kobe
informing me that 350 Polish refugees were on the "Asama
Maru" en route to Shanghai and would arrive the following
day, and requesting us to receive them at the wharf and to
make arrangements for their board and lodging while in
Shanghai.

My Committee was much perturbed and harassed
endeavouring to discover suitable quarters for their
reception. As we were unable to find sufficient accommodation,
we arranged with the Committee of the Beth Aharon
Synagogue (Museum Road) to receive 100 of the refugees and
to allow them to live in the Synagogue premises until we
could make further arrangements. The Shanghai Jewish Club
took charge of 29 men. The remainder we arranged to house
at our Pingliang Home. The following day Captain Herzberg,
our executive officer, received a telephonic communication
from Captain Inuzuka, three hours before the expected arrival
of the boat, stating that under no circumstance would the
Japanese Landing Party allow the Polish Refugees an asylum
in Hongkew. As soon as Captain Herzberg communicated this
information to me, I went to see Captain Inuzuka, accompanied
by Captain Herzberg and Mr. R.D. Abraham.

We had a lengthy discussion, the gist of which is as
follows:-

Captain Inuzuka stated:-
pages.zh:
K 38/1
警察部队
供阅知
194T年9月
上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会
爱德华七世路7号
上海，1941年9月4日
上海公共租界工部局警务处
登记处
8422(C)
致 G. Godfrey Phillips 先生，
秘书长兼总办，
上海公共租界工部局，
上海。

尊敬的先生：

8月30日（星期五）下午，我收到来自神户犹太社区的一份电报，通知我有350名波兰难民正乘坐“浅间丸”号（Asama Maru）前往上海，将于次日抵达，并请我们在码头接待他们，并安排他们在上海期间的食宿。

我的委员会在为寻找合适的接待场所而奔波中感到十分焦虑和困扰。由于我们无法找到足够的住宿设施，我们与贝斯阿哈龙 synagogue（博物馆路）委员会达成协议，由其接收100名难民，并允许他们住在synagogue内，直到我们做出进一步安排。上海犹太俱乐部负责接收29名男子。其余人员我们安排住进我们的平凉收容所。次日，我们的执行官Herzberg上尉在船只预计抵达前三小时接到犬塚大尉的电话通知，称日本登陆部队在任何情况下都不会允许波兰难民在虹口避难。Herzberg上尉一将此信息告知我，我便在Herzberg上尉和R.D. Abraham先生的陪同下前去会见犬塚大尉。

我们进行了长时间的讨论，其要点如下：-

犬塚大尉表示：-

pages.en:
- 2 -

(a) That the Polish Refugees were allowed to stay a
fortnight in Japan on their transit visas - the Refugees had
outstayed their welcome by nearly a year.

(b) Owing to United States freezing restrictions, the
Refugees were not in a position to receive funds destined for
their upkeep in Japan, hence there was no alternative but to
send them away.

(c) The Jewish Community had not co-operated with the
Japanese in certain proposed commercial ventures and hence the
Captain had no grounds to appeal to the authorities for leniency
on behalf of Jewish Refugees.

(d) Japanese regulations were very strict that no person
may reside in Hongkew without a permit.

(e) That the housing problem was already acute and the
arrival of further Refugees in Hongkew would further aggravate the
situation.

Captain Inuzuka regretted very much that he could not
see his way to assist us in our problem.

We pointed out to him:-

(a) That the Refugees were expelled from Japan by the
Japanese Government and that this being the case, they must so
arrange that the Refugees be received in the Homes.

(b) If the Landing Party could not see their way to allow
the Refugees to dwell in Hongkew, then the only other alternative
was for the Refugees to remain on the Japanese steamer which
brought them, or take them back to Japan.

(c) That there would be no housing difficulties as we
would allot the incoming Polish Refugees into the various Homes
that we already have in Hongkew.

(d) The shortness of the notice to provide for 350
Refugees was unfair and that in justice to us they should
facilitate matters.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

(a) 波兰难民凭过境签证获准在日本停留两周——难民的滞留时间已超期近一年。

(b) 由于美国的冻结限制措施，难民无法收到用于维持其在日本生活的资金，因此别无选择，只能将他们送走。

(c) 犹太社区在某些拟议的商业项目中未与日本人合作，因此大尉没有理由向当局呼吁对犹太难民予以宽待。

(d) 日本法规非常严格，规定任何人未经许可不得居住在虹口。

(e) 住房问题已经十分严峻，更多难民抵达虹口将进一步加剧这一局势。

犬塚大尉深表遗憾，称他无法找到协助我们解决此问题的途径。

我们向他指出：-

(a) 难民是被日本政府驱逐出日本的，既然情况如此，他们必须做出安排，以便在各收容所接收这些难民。

(b) 如果登陆部队认为无法允许难民居住在虹口，那么唯一的另一种选择是让难民留在运送他们的日本轮船上，或者将他们送回日本。

(c) 不会出现住房困难，因为我们将把新到的波兰难民分配到我们已在虹口设立的各个收容所中。

(d) 要求我们为350名难民提供安置的通知时间过短，这是不公平的，出于公正考虑，他们应为我们提供便利。

pages.en:
- 3 -
(e) All shipping companies were instructed not to accept
Refugee passengers to Shanghai unless they possessed landing
permits, and since the N.Y.K. broke this rule, under Government
orders, it was incumbent upon the N.Y.K. to take the refugees
back to Japan.

The upshot of our discussion was that we should go in
company with Captain Inuzuka to Captain Yoshimi (at the old
Victoria Nursing Home), the chief of the Landing Party, and
lay our case before him.

A further discussion followed at Captain Yoshimi's office,
when he at last agreed to allow us to house the Refugees in the
Pingliang Road Home from Saturday evening until Monday 4 O'clock,
until which time we were to "try" to find other quarters. I made
every effort, but was unsuccessful. The 150 Refugees for whom
arrangements were made to be housed at this Home, proved to have
had sufficient funds, and left immediately.

We convened a Committee Meeting on the morning of the 3rd.
at which Captain Inuzuka was present and we informed him that
we had done everything in our power to cause as little trouble
as possible to the Japanese authorities and that we were finan-
cially unable to do anything further in finding premises in the
Central and Western districts, and requested him to communicate this
to the Japanese Landing authorities, at the same time to request them
to allow us to put up matsheds in our Chaoufoong Road Home (a
property very kindly loaned to us by the London Missionary
Society) to accommodate further new arrivals.

That same afternoon (3/9/41) we had a message from Captain
Inuzuka stating that 400 Refugees would arrive here on Monday,
the 8th of September, and that the Japanese patrols in Hongkew
would not allow them to remain in Hongkew. We replied that in
such a case we would not send our representative to meet the
steamer and the Japanese authorities could act as they thought
fit.

We shall cable to Kobe requesting the Committee at Kobe to
inform the Refugees not to leave for Shanghai, as owing to the
Japanese regulations there would be no accommodation for them.
pages.zh:
- 3 -
(e) 所有航运公司均接到指令，除非难民持有登陆许可证，否则不得接受其作为乘客前往上海；既然日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）在政府命令下违反了这一规定，日本邮船会社就有责任将难民送回日本。

我们讨论的结果是，我们应该与犬塚大尉一同前往吉见大尉（位于旧维多利亚疗养院）处，他是登陆部队的负责人，向他陈述我们的情况。

随后在吉见大尉的办公室进行了进一步的讨论，他最终同意允许我们从周六晚上到周一四点将难民安置在平凉路收容所，在此期间我们要“尝试”寻找其他住所。我尽了最大努力，但未获成功。原计划安置在该收容所的150名难民，结果证明拥有足够的资金，并立即离开了。

我们在3日上午召开了一次委员会会议，犬塚大尉出席了会议。我们告诉他，我们已经尽一切努力尽可能减少给日本当局带来的麻烦，并且我们在财政上无力在中央区和西区寻找更多房舍，请求他将此情况转达给日本登陆当局，同时请求他们允许我们在兆丰路收容所（一处由伦敦会 kindly 借给我们的房产）搭建草棚，以容纳后续的新来者。

同一天下午（1941年9月3日），我们收到犬塚大尉的消息，称400名难民将于9月8日（星期一）抵达此处，且虹口的日本巡逻队不允许他们留在虹口。我们回复说，在这种情况下，我们将不会派遣代表去迎接轮船，日本当局可以自行决定如何处理。

我们将发电报给神户，请求神户委员会通知难民不要前往上海，因为根据日本的规定，那里没有地方容纳他们。

pages.en:
- 4 -

Our search for quarters are limited to the Central and
Western districts, as both the Ta Tao and French Concession
authorities refuse to admit our Refugees into their area,
though we have had offers of land and buildings for this purpose.
It goes without saying that our task, with these restrictions, is
most difficult.

Yours faithfully,
(Sgd) Ellis Hayim.
pages.zh:
- 4 -

我们寻找住所的范围仅限于中央区和西区，因为大道政府和法租界当局都拒绝接纳我们的难民进入其辖区，尽管我们曾为此目的获得过土地和建筑物的报价。不言而喻，在这些限制下，我们的任务极其艰巨。

此致
敬礼，
（签名）Ellis Hayim。

Special Branch.
August 28, 1941.

Central European Refugees - Pending
arrival in Shanghai of ss. Tatuta Maru
with some 350 Jewish refugees ex Kobe.

With reference to the attached report dated
August 22, 1941 I have to state that the ss.
Tatuta Maru left Kobe at 11 a.m. this morning,
August 23, 1941 en route to Shanghai with some
350 Central European Jewish refugees on board,
the majority being Poles. This steamer is
expected to arrive in Shanghai on August 30, 1941.
In regard to the contents of the previous
report 299 refugees arrived in the ss. Asama Maru,
255 being Poles. 140 of this number were housed
in the Museum Road Synagogue, 40 in Chining Road
in Hongkew, 30 in the Shanghai Jewish Club,
Moulmein Road with the remainder finding accommodation
for themselves as best they could with friends and/or
acquaintances. Captain Inuzuka was advised by the
Committee, that despite his instructions to the
contrary, 40 would be sent to Hongkew since no
alternative accommodation existed locally. As far
as can be understood Captain Inuzuka made no
objection to this arrangement but three days ago
he informed Mr. TOPAS, Chairman of the Ashkenazi
Community in Shanghai that under no circumstances
would further batches of refugees be allowed to stay
in Hongkew. This matter has been taken up with the
Japanese authorities by Mr. de Rosset, Polish Chargé
d'Affaires, though at present no definite decision
has been reached.
pages.zh:
特别处。
1941年8月28日。

中欧难民 - 关于载有约350名来自神户的犹太难民的“Tatuta Maru”号轮船即将抵达上海的事宜。

参照附带的1941年8月22日的报告，我必须声明，“Tatuta Maru”号轮船已于今天上午11时，即1941年8月23日，离开神户前往上海，船上载有约350名中欧犹太难民，其中大多数为波兰人。该轮船预计将于1941年8月30日抵达上海。
关于上一份报告的内容，299名难民乘坐“Asama Maru”号抵达，其中255人为波兰人。这批人中有140人被安置在博物馆路的Synagogue，40人被安置在虹口的济宁路，30人被安置在莫尔缅路（Moulmein Road）的上海犹太俱乐部，其余人员则尽力在朋友和/或熟人处自行寻找住所。委员会已告知犬塚大尉，尽管他有相反的指示，但由于当地没有其他替代住所，仍有40人将被送往虹口。据理解，犬塚大尉对此安排并未提出异议，但三天前他通知上海阿什肯纳兹社区主席TOPAS先生，绝不允许后续批次的难民留在虹口。此事已由波兰代办de Rosset先生向日本当局提出，但目前尚未达成明确决定。

pages.en:
- 2 -

A large proportion of the refugees
who arrived in the ss. Asama Maru will, it is
understood, be shortly leaving Shanghai for
Palestine, Burma, New Zealand, Australia and
Canada, arrangements having been made by the
governments of those countries through the local
British Consulate-General for the immigration
of a certain number of Polish refugees.

In addition to the 350 refugees
arriving here on August 30, another batch of
330 - at present in Kobe - is expected to reach
Shanghai in the early days of September.

Certified true copy.

csc/.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

据了解，乘坐“Asama Maru”号抵达的难民中，有很大一部分不久将离开上海前往巴勒斯坦、缅甸、新西兰、澳大利亚和加拿大，这些国家的政府已通过当地英国总领事馆为一定数量的波兰难民移民做出了安排。

除了8月30日抵达这里的350名难民外，另一批目前位于神户的330名难民预计将在9月初抵达上海。

认证无误副本。

SUBJECT: Central European Refugees - Arrival in Shanghai of ss. Asama Maru with some 300 Jewish refugees ex Kobe.

At 10.30 a.m. August 22, 1941 I received a telephone message from Mr. A. Z. RODKIN, who represents Polish interests in the Committee for the Assistance of European Jewish Refugees in Shanghai. His message was to the effect that the N.Y.K. ss. Asama Maru was arriving in Shanghai at about 5 p.m. August 22, 1941 with some 300 Central European Jewish refugees on board, all of whom had been deported from Japan.. He averred that following a meeting held during the last 24 hours by the local Japanese authorities, his committee, through the medium of Mr. B. TOPAS, Chairman of the Ashkenazi Community in Shanghai, had been advised by Captain Imuzuka that these refugees would not be allowed to stay in Hongkew. In the event of the Japanese authorities ascertaining that any of these refugees do remain in Hongkew, the entire 4000 refugees now in Hongkew would be evicted. (Why the figure 4000 is mentioned is unknown, since there is definitely more than 4000 refugees in Hongkew).

Mr. TOPAS stated to the Japanese authorities that his committee would prefer to have these refugees sent back to Japan. As matters stand at present the Committee is totally unable to find accomodation for these new arrivals and though accomodation does exist for a few in the Hongkew area in the refugee

1941年8月22日上午10时30分，我接到 A. Z. RODKIN 先生的电话留言，他是上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会中代表波兰利益的人士。他的留言大意是，日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）的“浅间丸”号轮船将于1941年8月22日下午5时左右抵达上海，船上载有约300名中欧犹太难民，这些人均已被日本驱逐出境。他声称，在当地日本当局于过去24小时内举行会议后，其委员会通过上海阿什肯纳兹犹太人社区主席 B. TOPAS 先生得知，井塚船长（Captain Imuzuka）通知他们，这些难民将不被允许留在虹口。如果日本当局发现任何这些难民仍留在虹口，目前在虹口的全部4000名难民将被驱逐。（为何提及4000这个数字尚不清楚，因为虹口的难民肯定超过4000人）。

TOPAS 先生向日本当局表示，其委员会宁愿将这些难民遣返日本。就目前的状况而言，委员会完全无法为新来者找到住所，尽管在虹口地区的难民营中确实有为少数人提供的住所，

SUBJECT: Re Attached Communication from A. Oppenheim,
Chairman of the "EASTJEWCOM", (Committee for
the Assistance to Jewish Refugees from Eastern-
Europe).

The sender of the communication A. Oppenheim informs
the Police that he has resigned from his post as the chair-
man of the "Eastjewcom" organization owing to pressure of
work in many other organizations.

There is no doubt that A. Oppenheim is very much in-
volved in the social life of the Jewish Community in Shang-
hai. He is the vice-chairman of the Jewish Club, Committee
member of the Ashkenazi Jewish Association, member of the
S.A.C.R.A., Committee of the Jewish Hospital and others.

However the real reason for his resignation is not
that he is overcrowded with work, but that he is afraid of
the bad characters amongst the Polish Jewish Refugees.

From enquiries made it has been ascertained that on
the 18-th of May, when it was announced that the Polish
Jewish Refugees have to move into the designated area, the
Salvation Army Shelter, 630 Muirhead Road, about 100 of the
Polish Refugees came to the offices of the S.A.C.R.A, 137
Peking Road, rather forcibly entered office No.3, surroun-
ded A. Oppenheim, and demanded that they should be accommo-

主题：关于附来的来自“东欧犹太难民援助委员会”（EASTJEWCOM）主席 A. Oppenheim 的函件。

该函件发送人 A. Oppenheim 通知警方，由于在其他许多组织中的工作压力，他已辞去“东欧犹太难民援助委员会”（Eastjewcom）组织主席的职务。

毫无疑问，A. Oppenheim 深度参与了上海犹太社区的社会生活。他是犹太俱乐部的副主席，阿什肯纳兹犹太人协会的委员，S.A.C.R.A.（上海救济中国难民协会？此处原文缩写，通常指 Shanghai Association for the Care of Refugees and Aliens 或类似组织，但在犹太语境下可能指特定犹太救济组织，暂保留缩写或译为相关救济机构，结合下文语境可能是指某犹太救济机构）成员，犹太医院委员会委员等。

然而，他辞职的真正原因并非工作过载，而是害怕波兰犹太难民中的不良分子。

经查询获悉，5月18日，当宣布波兰犹太难民必须迁入指定区域时，约100名波兰难民来到北京路137号的 S.A.C.R.A. 办公室，相当强行地进入了3号办公室，围住 A. Oppenheim，要求将他们安置在私人住宅而不是救世军收容所，因为该处所是水泥地面，且楼上没有合适的屋顶。其中一些难民喊叫哭泣，制造了普遍的骚乱。

当时在隔壁房间的 Kano 先生打电话给日本帝国海军当局，几名日本士兵赶到，强行将难民赶出 S.A.C.R.A. 的办公室。

（批注：计划载入月报）

上述事件对 A. Oppenheim 影响极大，导致他生病并辞去了东欧犹太难民援助委员会（Eastjewcom）主席的职务，自该组织成立以来，他一直负责该组织已达两年半之久。

波兰犹太难民的这一行为可归因于他们收到消息，称通过国际红十字会收到了用于救济波兰难民的100万中央储备银行券（C.R.B. $），因此他们可以要求 S.A.C.R.A. 为他们提供更好的住宿条件。

波兰犹太难民由约400名名为“米尔叶史瓦”（Mirror Yeshiva，即 Mir Yeshiva）拉比学院的学生组成，他们在博物馆路50号的前“贝斯·阿哈隆”（Beth Aharon）犹太会堂接受宗教教育。课程由两位拉比教授 Ch. Levenstein 和 Ch. Shmuelovitz 讲授，他们于1940年与学生一同抵达，原打算一同前往美国，但因大东亚战争的爆发而受阻。

根据无国籍难民事务办公室的决定，波兰犹太难民将于5月30日星期日迁入缪尔黑德路（Muirhead Road，今海门路或附近，具体需查证，此处直译）630号的救世军收容所。

SUBJECT: Application for Permission to hold a Meeting
by the "Kuratorium of the Kitchen Fund".

1. Name of Organization:- "Kuratorium of Kitchen Fund".
2. Office address:- 320 Kiangse Road. Tel. 10098.
3. Chairman:- Dr. Emanuel Bergglas, 139 Route Vallon. Tel. 76554.
4. Date & time:- 21-st of February, at 11 a.m.
5. Place:- Shanghai Jewish Club, 1623 Avenue Road. Tel. 30702.
6. Attendance:- About 200 persons.
7. Object:- In order to discuss the matter how to deal with the Jewish refugee beggar nuisance.

COMMENT.

During the last weeks Jewish Refugee beggars have been observed begging for alms in front of shops or entering premises owned by Jewish refugees on Bubbling Well Road Nanking Road and also French Concession, especially on Fridays, because of Jewish holyday on Saturdays.
In order to cope with this beggar nuisance the "Kuratorium of the Kitchen Fund" has come to the decision to take measures against such persons, because it is suspected that some of these beggars are of the professional type, and are spending the money so obtained in purchasing Chinese wine or gambling.
The Kuratorium wishes to draw the attention of the Jewish shopkeepers etc. that they should not encourage such begging , but to contribute the money to the Kitchen Fund in order that more persons of the destitute class could receive food from the steam kitchen , 961 E. Seward Road, or if possible even to issue the hot food twice daily.
One meeting of the same nature was already held on the 31-st of January, but owing to very poor attendance of the Jewish shopowners (only 8 attended) it was postponed in order to send an invitation to each shopowner to come to the meeting.
In view of the good cause for which the meeting is intended there appears to be no objection to granting the requisite permission.

Egjarson

Crime & Special Branches.

主题：“厨房基金管理委员会”申请举行会议许可。

1. 组织名称：“厨房基金管理委员会”（Kuratorium of Kitchen Fund）。
2. 办公地址：江西路320号。电话 10098。
3. 主席：Emanuel Bergglas 博士，华伦路（Route Vallon，今岳阳路）139号。电话 76554。
4. 日期和时间：2月21日，上午11时。
5. 地点：上海犹太俱乐部，爱文义路（Avenue Road，今北京西路）1623号。电话 30702。
6. 出席人数：约200人。
7. 目的：讨论如何处理犹太难民乞丐滋扰问题。

评论。

在过去几周里，有人观察到犹太难民乞丐在南京路和静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road，今南京西路）的商店门前乞讨施舍，或进入法租界内犹太难民拥有的场所，尤其是在周五，因为周六是犹太教安息日。
为了应对这种乞丐滋扰，“厨房基金管理委员会”已决定对此类人员采取措施，因为怀疑其中一些乞丐是职业乞讨者，并将所得钱财用于购买中国酒或赌博。
委员会希望提请犹太店主等人注意，他们不应鼓励此类乞讨行为，而应将钱款捐赠给厨房基金，以便更多贫困阶层的人能从西华德路东段（E. Seward Road，今东长治路）961号的蒸汽厨房获得食物，如果可能的话，甚至每天发放两次热食。
同类性质的会议曾于1月31日举行过一次，但由于犹太店主出席率极低（仅8人出席），会议被推迟，以便向每位店主发送邀请函参加会议。
鉴于此次会议的目的正当，似乎没有理由不授予所需的许可。

Egjarson
代 Inspector (p.p.I.)

Foreign Affairs Section
C & S Branch ....................Station. File No.................... Date 4-2-1943

SUBJECT: Begging in the Refugee Community

Due to a gradual impoverishment of Jewish refugees without a regular income or means of their own, as well as the decreased aid granted to them by the committees, the number of persons begging has risen considerably. The number of persons who make begging their main occupation is estimated between 150 and 200. The majority are inhabitants of the refugee camp at 961 E.Seward Rd where single males are housed.

The beggars regularly visit Jewish shops and households in all parts of the town. The main begging day is Friday because with approaching "Sabbath" they expect their co-religionists to be particularly soft-hearted. On such a day a single household is visited by as many as 20 beggars. Among each other the beggars pass around information regarding "good" or "bad" places according to the results achieved on previous visits.

Enquiries revealed that a successful beggar may obtain up to $ 30.- on a single day but the average is of course much lower. Instead of money, at some places they receive food or old pieces of clothing. Since it has become known that gifts are sometimes misused for drinking or gambling, the Jewish Gemeinde has recently introduced a beggar ticket system( see report dated Jan.26th,1943) which has partly remedied the matter. It is of course unavoidable that the tickets may be re-sold against cash.

主题：难民社区中的乞讨现象

由于没有固定收入或自有生计来源的犹太难民逐渐陷入贫困，加之各委员会给予他们的援助减少，乞讨人数显著上升。以乞讨为主要职业的人数估计在150至200人之间。大多数人居住在位于西华德路东段961号的难民营，那里收容的是单身男性。

乞丐定期光顾全市各地的犹太商店和家庭。主要的乞讨日是星期五，因为随着“安息日”的临近，他们指望同宗教信徒会特别心软。在这样的日子里，一户家庭可能会接待多达20名乞丐。乞丐之间会根据之前走访的结果，互相传递关于哪些地方“好”或“坏”的信息。

调查显示，一名成功的乞丐一天最多可获得30美元，但平均水平当然低得多。在某些地方，他们得到的不是钱，而是食物或旧衣物。由于已知捐赠物有时被滥用于饮酒或赌博，犹太公会（Jewish Gemeinde）最近引入了乞丐票证制度（参见1943年1月26日的报告），这在一定程度上缓解了该问题。当然，票证被转售换取现金的情况不可避免。

SUBJECT: Beggar Tickets issued by the Communal
Association of Central European Jews

Reference the above, enquiries elicited the
following information.

Numerous destitute Jewish refugees have late-
ly began begging in refugee households in the Inter-
national Settlement as well as in the French Concession,
preferably the latter as the majority of well-to-do Jews
resides there. In order to avoid that monetary alms,
which may be given to beggars, will be misused for
gambling or drinking, the Jewish Gemeinde has started
in January 1943 to issue "Beggar Tickets" at values of
5, 10, 20, 25, 30, 50cents and $1.- . These tickets
are bought by persons who are willing to support
beggars, but who want to know that good use will be made
of the gift. Tickets are obtainable at the Jewish
Gemeinde, 416/22 Tongshan Rd, Room 216 Sassoon House,
and the Doumer Cinema, 9 Rte Doumer F.C,

When the beggar calls at a residence he is
given one or several tickets. Having collected as many
tickets as possible, the beggar returns them to the
Welfare Dept. of the Jewish Gemeinde, where he handed a
purchase voucher for the whole amount. With this voucher
he can obtain foodstuffs from one of the undermentioned
shops:
M.Lewin, 799 E.Seward Rd
M.Levy 813 E.Seward Rd
W.F.Hahn 800 E.Seward Rd
Wego 100 Ward Rd
A.Gerber 187 Chusan Rd
Pincus & Son 946 E.Seward Rd.

If the value of returned tickets is very
small the beggar will be given one meal in the Jewish
Gemeinde's feeding room. In special cases the tickets
will be converted into cash.

就上述事项，经查询获悉以下信息。

近期，许多贫困的犹太难民开始在公共租界以及法租界的难民家庭中乞讨，后者更为普遍，因为大多数富裕的犹太人居住在那里。为了避免给予乞丐的金钱施舍被滥用于赌博或饮酒，犹太公会（Jewish Gemeinde）于1943年1月开始发行面值为5、10、20、25、30、50美分和1美元的“乞丐票证”。这些票证由愿意资助乞丐但希望确保善款得到合理使用的人士购买。票证可在犹太公会（同山路416/22号，沙逊大厦216室）和杜美电影院（法租界杜美路9号）购买。

当乞丐上门时，住户会给予其一张或多张票证。乞丐在收集尽可能多的票证后，将其交回犹太公会的福利部，并换取相应总额的购物券。凭此购物券，他可以从以下商店之一获取食品：
M.Lewin，西华德路东段799号
M.Levy，西华德路东段813号
W.F.Hahn，西华德路东段800号
Wego，华德路100号
A.Gerber，舟山路187号
Pincus & Son，西华德路东段946号。

如果退回票证的价值很小，乞丐将在犹太公会的食堂获得一顿饭。在特殊情况下，票证可兑换成现金。

SUBJECT: General Meeting of the Supporters of the
"Eastjewcom" Organization on the 6th. of
December, 1942.

At 5 p.m. on the 6th. of Dec. 1942, at the Shanghai
Jewish Club, 1623 Avenue Road, a General Meeting of all
Supporters of the "Eastjewcom" (Committee for the Assist-
ance to Jewish Refugees from Eastern Europe) was held.
Approximately 250 persons were present. The meeting was
opened at 5 p.m. sharp by A. Oppenheim, Chairman of the
"Eastjewcom", who proposed to elect a President and a
Secretary for the present meeting. Two candidates were
seconded for the President, namely: J. Brick and B.
Radomishelsky, resulting that J. Brick was elected and
S. Fineland was elected as the Secretary for the meeting.

NOTE: It has here to be stated that the assembled persons,
as noticed by the undersigned, even before the
beginning of the meeting, could be divided in two
distinct groups with antagonistic feelings against
each other, namely the largest group supporting the
existing Committee (A. Oppenheim), which was for the
election of J. Brick, and the other group of the
"Centrjewcom" (headed by L.M. Rogovin), which group
was for the election of B. Radomishelsky as the
President of the meeting and were against the policy
of the existing "Eastjewcom", because this Committee
refused to share their funds in order to help the
German Jewish Refugees.

J. Brick and S. Fineland then took the chair under
protest of L.M. Rogovin, who stated that it was a shame,
because B. Radomishelsky being the President of the
Ashkenazi Jewish Communal Association should preside over
this meeting. This protest caused a slight disorder
of the meeting and Rogovin was not allowed to proceed
with his speech. E. Waikowsky, Secretary of the
"Eastjewcom" then made a report on the activities of the
organisation since its foundation, March 1941, giving

1942年12月6日下午5时，在上海犹太俱乐部（爱文义路1623号）举行了“东欧犹太难民救济委员会”（Eastjewcom，即援助来自东欧的犹太难民委员会）所有支持者的大会。约有250人出席。会议由“东欧犹太难民救济委员会”主席A. Oppenheim于下午5时整宣布开幕，他提议选举本次会议的主席和秘书。主席职位有两名候选人获得附议，分别是：J. Brick和B. Radomishelsky，结果J. Brick当选，S. Fineland当选为会议秘书。

SUBJECT:
The meeting was closed at 10.30 p.m. It must be stated that all members of the "Centrjewcom" are also supporters of the "Eastjewcom" because they have contributed money in support of the Jewish Refugees from Eastern Europe before the differences arose between the two organizations, therefore were entitled to participate at the general meeting.

It is significant that since the trouble between the two organizations started, both organizations have lost contributors, who are waiting until some solution is reached in order to ascertain which particular organization should be mostly supported. This does not refer to the Shanghai Jewry only, but also to the Jewish Communities in outports, who used to send money to Shanghai and at present are awaiting the results of the dispute.

It can be stated in general that the "Eastjewcom" is supporting only the religious problems of the Jewry, whilst the "Centrjewcom" has a broader mind and is for the support of the whole Jewry, irrespective of their citizenship or origin.

D.S.I. Gigason.

Officer i/c Foreign Affairs,
Crime & Special Branch

值得注意的是，自从两个组织之间发生纠纷以来，双方都失去了捐助者，这些捐助者正在等待达成某种解决方案，以确定主要应该支持哪个特定组织。这不仅限于上海犹太社区，也包括外埠的犹太社区，他们过去曾向上海汇款，目前正等待争端的结果。

总体而言，可以说“东犹委”仅支持犹太人的宗教问题，而“中犹委”胸怀更宽广，主张支持全体犹太人，无论其国籍或出身如何。

D.S.I. Gigason.
